body: We introduce NanoProof, to our knowledge the first factorized execution-guided theorem prover in Lean 4 whose training data, extraction tooling, training pipeline, and weights are all released, making it end-to-end reproducible using open-source resources. To this end, we build and release a dataset of structured proof trees, as well as a tool for programmatic interaction and data extraction within the Lean 4 formal verifier. To support sustainable research, we focus on compute efficiency to facilitate accessible training and evaluation. NanoProof achieves 50.8% pass@16 on MiniF2F-Test, exceeding the two closest systems of its class, HyperTree Proof Search and ABEL, at roughly 90x and 7x less compute, and using more than four orders of magnitude less compute than AlphaProof. Stronger open-weight provers exist, but they are fine-tuned from large pretrained language models and release neither training data nor pipeline; NanoProof shows that the factorized execution-guided class of provers can be rebuilt from scratch with modest resources.
summaryZh: 该研究发布了NanoProof，据称是首个在Lean 4中实现的、完全开源且可端到端复现的因子化执行引导式定理证明器。研究团队发布了其训练数据、提取工具、训练流程和模型权重，并构建了一个用于在Lean 4中进行程序化交互和数据提取的工具。NanoProof在MiniF2F-Test基准上达到了50.8%的pass@16，性能优于现有最接近的系统，同时计算量仅为其几十分之一甚至几百分之一。该项目强调了计算效率的重要性，旨在促进可及的训练和评估，并证明了因子化执行引导式证明器可以从零开始、以适度资源构建。
